title: DFIR Analyst
description: Investigate complex security breaches, perform digital forensics, analyze memory artifacts, preserve chain of custody, and remediate incidents.

goal.objective: Uncover the root cause of security incidents, extract forensic evidence from endpoints and memory, and guide organizations through emergency containment.

learn.summary: Master volatile memory extraction and analysis with Volatility, Windows forensic artifacts (MFT, Registry, Prefetch, Event Logs), disk imaging, and timeline analysis with Plaso.
key_competencies: Evidence Handling & Legal Chain of Custody

capstone_projects.title: Enterprise Ransomware Breach Investigation & Timeline Reconstruction
capstone_projects.description: Perform an end-to-end memory and disk forensic investigation of a simulated enterprise ransomware intrusion, reconstructing adversary lateral movement.

capstone_projects.title: Automated Endpoint Forensic Triage & YARA Threat Hunting Harness
capstone_projects.description: Deploy an automated live-response artifact triage system using Velociraptor VQL queries and custom YARA memory scanners across 100+ simulated endpoints.

interview_focus: Windows Forensic Artifacts ($MFT, USN Journal, Shimcache, Amcache, Prefetch, Shellbags)
Memory Forensics (VAD Tree Analysis, Code Injection, Process Hollow Detection)
Order of Volatility & Forensic Evidence Handling (Chain of Custody, Hash Verification)
Event Log Analysis (Sysmon Events 1, 3, 7, 8, 10, Security Events 4624, 4672, 4720)
Reconstructing Adversary Lateral Movement (Pass-the-Ticket, WMI, PsExec, RDP Tunnels)

tree.name: DFIR Fundamentals & Incident Response Lifecycle
tree.description: Master Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) principles, the NIST SP 800-61 / ISO 27035 incident lifecycles, chain of custody verification, and forensic lab engineering.

resources.title: NIST Incident Handling Guide SP 800-61 Rev. 2
Git and GitHub for Beginners - Crash Course
Incident Response Full Course - Learn to Protect Your Systems from Cyber Attacks

children.name: Incident Response Life Cycle & Frameworks
children.description: Execute every phase of the Incident Response lifecycle: Preparation, Detection & Analysis, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, and Post-Incident Activity. Establish enterprise containment and communication playbooks.

resources.title: Understanding the NIST Incident Response Life Cycle
Incident Response Playbooks: What Are They & How to Create One
What is an Incident Response Plan? (NIST 800-61 Explained)

children.name: Digital Forensics Principles & Evidence Handling
children.description: Enforce strict forensic standards: Adhere to RFC 3227 order of volatility, maintain verifiable cryptographic chain of custody (MD5/SHA256), avoid live evidence contamination, and manage legally defensible exhibits.

resources.title: ACPO Good Practice Guide for Digital Evidence
Digital Forensics for Beginners | Intro to Cybersecurity

children.name: DFIR Lab Setup & Essential Tooling
children.description: Build an isolated DFIR lab environment: Deploy SIFT Workstation, REMnux, forensic hardware write-blockers, virtualized analysis networks, and evidence repository servers.

resources.title: KAPE (Kroll Artifact Parser and Extractor) Documentation
Git and GitHub for Beginners - Crash Course

children.name: Operating System Fundamentals for Forensics
children.description: Master operating system internals for forensics: Windows kernel architecture, NTFS/FAT/ReFS file systems, Linux ext4/XFS metadata, processes, memory management, and system call execution flows.

resources.title: System Design Concepts Course and Interview Prep
Linux Kernel Internals - A Crash Course

tree.name: Core Technical Skills & Implementation
tree.description: Execute live incident response, host forensic artifact extraction, volatile memory forensics, and deep network packet analysis across Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms.

resources.title: Digital Forensics Course - Learn the Basics of Computer Forensics

children.name: Live Response & Endpoint Triage
children.description: Perform rapid live host triage: Collect volatile endpoint data using KAPE, CyLR, and Velociraptor; capture running processes, network sockets, loaded modules, logged-on users, and scheduled tasks without altering state.

resources.title: Introduction to Live Response with Kansa
Live Response for Incident Response & Threat Hunting
Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) Master Class 2026

children.name: Windows Host Forensics
children.description: Analyze critical Windows forensic artifacts using Eric Zimmerman tools: Master File Table ($MFT, $LogFile), Registry hives (SYSTEM, SOFTWARE, NTUSER.dat), Shimcache, Amcache, Prefetch, SRUM, and Event Logs (EVTX).

resources.title: The Windows Registry: A Forensic Perspective
Windows Forensics Crash Course Part 1 - Windows Artifacts
DFIR: Windows Host Forensics - Tools and Artifacts

children.name: Linux & macOS Host Forensics
children.description: Investigate Linux and macOS endpoints: Analyze `/var/log` artifacts, systemd journals, cron jobs, bash history, auditd logs, Unified Logs (OSLog), LaunchDaemons, LaunchAgents, and extended file attributes.

resources.title: macOS Incident Response and Forensics with Phil Hagen

children.name: File System Forensics Deep Dive
children.description: Dissect file systems at the byte and cluster level: Analyze NTFS attributes ($STANDARD_INFORMATION, $FILE_NAME), timestamp resolution, timestomping detection, alternate data streams (ADS), and unallocated space carvers.

resources.title: Digital Forensics and Incident Response: Mastering NTFS
Master File Table (MFT) Deep Dive | DFIR
Deep Dive into Linux Filesystems (ext4) and Forensics

children.name: Memory Forensics
children.description: Perform advanced volatile memory analysis with Volatility 3 and Rekall: Acquire RAM dumps via LiME/WinPmem, identify injected DLLs, unhooked code, hidden processes (DKOM), extract network sockets, and dump process memory.

children.name: Network Forensics & Packet Analysis
children.description: Investigate network evidence: Deep packet inspection (PCAP) with Wireshark and Zeek (Bro); reconstruct TCP streams, extract transmitted files, identify C2 beaconing patterns, and analyze NetFlow/IPFIX telemetry.

resources.title: Wireshark Tutorial for Beginners - Network Analysis

children.name: Log Analysis & SIEM Fundamentals
children.description: Correlate multi-source enterprise logs in SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Sentinel): Query Windows security events (4624, 4688, 4720), Sysmon events (1, 3, 7, 8, 10), firewall logs, and reverse proxy access records.

resources.title: The ELK Stack: A Deep Dive into Logs
Getting Started with SIEM | Security Information and Event Management Explained
ELK Stack Tutorial - ELK Stack Explained

tree.name: Advanced DFIR & Operational Excellence
tree.description: Architect enterprise incident orchestration, proactive threat hunting, cloud and container forensics, malware triage, and automated DFIR scripting.

resources.title: Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) Master Class (Prabh Nair)

children.name: Enterprise IR & SOAR Automation
children.description: Design enterprise-wide Incident Response orchestration: Integrate SOAR platforms (Cortex XSOAR, Splunk SOAR), automate host quarantine, revoke session tokens, and coordinate cross-functional crisis management.

resources.title: What is SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response)?
Python Automation Tutorial for Beginners (Full Course)

children.name: Threat Hunting & MITRE ATT&CK
children.description: Execute proactive hypothesis-driven threat hunting: Map enterprise telemetry gaps against MITRE ATT&CK, author custom Sigma and YARA-L rules, and sweep endpoints for elusive adversary persistence.

resources.title: Threat Hunting 101: What it is and How to get Started

children.name: Cloud & Container Forensics
children.description: Forensicate cloud and container environments: Collect and analyze AWS CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty findings, Azure Activity/Sign-in logs, GCP Audit logs, and inspect ephemeral Kubernetes pod snapshots.

children.name: Malware Triage & Basic Analysis
children.description: Perform rapid malware triage on collected artifacts: Extract strings, calculate fuzzy hashes (SSDEEP), inspect imported API symbols, unpack compressed payloads, and execute safe dynamic detonation in Cuckoo Sandbox.

resources.title: REMnux: The Linux Toolkit for Reverse-Engineering and Malware Analysis
YARA: The Pattern Matching Swiss Knife for Malware Researchers
Malware Analysis Crash Course for Beginners
YARA Rules Tutorial For Beginners | Create & Test YARA Rules

children.name: Scripting for DFIR Automation
children.description: Automate forensic processing using Python and PowerShell: Develop automated scripts to parse EVTX logs, query MFT databases, extract timeline artifacts with Plaso/log2timeline, and automate IOC hashing.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
Python Automation Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course
PowerShell for Beginners Course - Learn in 4 Hours

children.name: Email Forensics
children.description: Investigate business email compromise (BEC) and phishing: Analyze raw RFC 5322 email headers, SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication verdicts, tracing originating IP hops, and extract weaponized macro attachments.

resources.title: Email Header Analysis For Phishing Investigations
Analyzing Phishing Emails with John Hammond

children.name: Advanced Threat Detection & Response
children.description: Detect and remediate advanced in-memory threats: Recognize Process Hollowing, Process Doppelgänging, AtomBombing, reflective DLL injection, and credential dumping (LSASS, DPAPI, NTDS.dit).

resources.title: Advanced Persistent Threats: A Practical Guide
Cyber Security: Threat Hunting - Learn to hunt for threats in your network
What is an APT attack? (Advanced Persistent Threat)

tree.name: Portfolio & Career Readiness
tree.description: Build a demonstrable DFIR portfolio: Document incident response simulation write-ups, contribute to open-source DFIR tools/parsers, and earn recognized certifications (GCFA, GCFE, GCIH).

resources.title: Building a Cybersecurity Portfolio (A Must-Have for Beginners)!
How to Get a Job in Cybersecurity (Tips, Tricks & Resources)

children.name: Incident Reporting & Stakeholder Communication
children.description: Author comprehensive forensic incident reports: Craft executive breach summaries, detailed technical timelines, root-cause analyses, chain-of-custody documentation, and regulatory remediation roadmaps.

resources.title: Cyber Security Incident Response: Communication Plan

children.name: DFIR Capstone Project: End-to-End Incident Simulation
children.description: Execute an enterprise DFIR capstone: Investigate a multi-stage simulated enterprise ransomware intrusion from initial phishing access through lateral movement and exfiltration, producing full timeline and eradication proof.

resources.title: Blue Team Labs Online - Incident Response Challenge Walkthrough
Incident Response in the Real World: The Basics

children.name: Career Development & Certifications
children.description: Navigate professional DFIR growth: Master legal expert witness testimony principles, stay current with DFIR research (SANS DFIR Summit, Black Hat), and pursue advanced credentials.

resources.title: Top DFIR Certifications for Your Career
How To Get Into DFIR (Digital Forensics & Incident Response)
